objective: Accurate, coverage-labelled observed lifecycle MCAP evidence without another provider client, executor, normalizer, journal, or scheduler.

existing_functionality.request_and_transport: token_data_provider_bindings.build_birdeye_ohlcv_request and BirdeyeProductionBinding provide the canonical V3 MCAP request and one-attempt transport.
existing_functionality.historical_executor: watchtower_historical_executor.HistoricalExecutor uses the canonical builder, 15m normalization, a durable six-range SQLite FSM, and capped attempts; it is not read-only or cohort-generic.
existing_functionality.terminal_finalizer: watchtower_terminal_ath_finalizer.WatchtowerTerminalAthFinalizer reuses contiguous retained 15m OHLC when available, otherwise requests chunked OHLC, validates coverage, calculates observed high, 2x/5x/10x crossings and peak-to-current-close drawdown, then writes canonical observations/facts.
existing_functionality.fact_reducer: watchtower_price_fact_contract.reduce_watchtower_price_facts provides ordered observed-peak, crossing, and close drawdown calculations only.
existing_functionality.retained_evidence: watchtower_15m_provider_evidence_liveness.v1.json proves 7 committed 15m candles for 2 mints; the opening dataset supplies compact one-hour extrema and coverage, not lifecycle paths.

reused_components: Canonical Birdeye V3 request builder and production binding.
Established full-OHLC timestamp/value normalization rules, subject to the documented contract mismatch audit.
reduce_watchtower_price_facts for ordered observed maxima, threshold crossings, and peak-to-close drawdown.
Existing runtime gate, shared 20-global/4-per-mint admission, compact evidence limits, and crash/no-repeat ownership boundaries.
unnecessary_duplication_identified: A second Birdeye client, endpoint contract, request builder, budget, scheduler, provider ledger, or canonical lifecycle calculator is unnecessary and prohibited.
The prior single-request lifecycle probe is not a cohort execution path and must not be expanded or retried.

current_lifecycle_data_available.fifteen_minute: Seven retained successful 15m observations over two mints; sparse and not cohort-wide lifecycle coverage.
not_available: Contiguous creation-to-last-observation OHLC paths for the Watchtower cohort.
Coverage-qualified lifecycle observed peaks, post-peak troughs, recoveries, or last observations for the cohort.
Evidence sufficient to call any observed peak a verified lifetime ATH or any last observation terminal valuation.

lifecycle_accuracy_assessment.units: The canonical request explicitly selects chart_type=mcap and currency=usd; direct provider MCAP values require validated positive-finite full OHLC fields before use.
lifecycle_accuracy_assessment.chronology: Existing reducer orders timestamped candles. It identifies an observed high, but it does not itself calculate peak-to-subsequent-trough or recovery peaks; those require a contiguous, coverage-qualified series and an explicitly qualified analysis layer.
lifecycle_accuracy_assessment.regimes: Creation/curve and post-migration AMM observations must remain separately labelled. Existing opening evidence cannot be blended into post-migration lifecycle extrema without a defined boundary.
lifecycle_accuracy_assessment.coverage: The finalizer rejects gaps for non-retained requests and labels sparse retained 15m results; it is therefore safer than treating HTTP 200 or a last row as coverage.

minimum_missing_capability: A non-canonical, cohort-scoped composition of existing terminal-finalizer/reducer logic with the existing shared runtime gate, admission, segmented no-repeat journal, compact evidence root, and a coverage-aware post-peak/recovery reducer. Existing finalizer only admits terminal facts and commits canonical SQLite rows; existing historical executor owns a different SQLite FSM and range contract. Configuration alone cannot change either persistence authority or derive post-peak trough/recovery metrics.

minimum_implementation_if_required.reuse: Call existing canonical request builder/binding, established normalizer, runtime gate, shared admission, segmented journal and price-fact reducer; do not copy them.
minimum_implementation_if_required.correction: Add only an isolated persistence adapter and coverage-aware lifecycle projection that consumes validated OHLC output. It must never write operation_monitor_facts or canonical observations.
minimum_implementation_if_required.provider_impact: None for qualification. Any future acquisition requires separate explicit request authority after retained-fixture normalization qualification.
minimum_implementation_if_required.storage: Compact derived milestones plus coverage diagnostics only; max 1MiB/artifact, explicit cohort cap at or below 100MiB, transient atomic overlap bounded, raw payload retention=false, and no design path to a 500MB file.
minimum_implementation_if_required.regression: Existing terminal adapter/executor/reducer tests plus isolated no-repeat, coverage-gap, peak-before-trough, recovery, and canonical-DB-isolation fixtures.

provider_request_estimate: Not responsibly quantifiable from retained evidence. Existing finalizer plans ceil((terminal_timestamp-entry_timestamp)/chunk_seconds) V3 requests per mint, while the historical executor permits at most 12 15m physical attempts plus one opening attempt. Neither bound proves lifecycle coverage or is authorized for this cohort.
recommended_execution_path: First use existing retained compact evidence for provider-free opening-hour and sparse-15m analysis only.
Do not use the canonical terminal finalizer or historical executor against live Watchtower state: both persist canonical SQLite records.

If lifecycle research remains required, authorize one minimal isolated composition that reuses the listed components, after a retained-fixture shared-normalizer qualification proves the exact provider contract.
next_gate: Stop. Do not acquire lifecycle data. A separately authorized retained-fixture normalizer qualification is the prerequisite to deciding whether the minimal isolated composition is justified.
